03What the centre did+

Materiality: revenue is the metric where a wrong assumption about the acquisition/non-comp contribution moves the answer by ~1.5 points of growth (~$700m), far more than anything the comp debate can move it. Views anchored to a reported run-rate that already contains that contribution, and to consensus which models it explicitly, therefore dominate a view that applies an annual guided midpoint uniformly across a quarter with a non-comparable base.

guidancepass5A quarter specific guidance statement from Home Depot for Q2 fiscal 2026, or at least two historical instances where the company gave a guided range and I could observe where the actual result landed within that range, would let me replace the midpoint assumption with an empirically derived landing position, likely shifting the estimates toward the low or high end depending on the pattern observed.

03What the centre did+

Materiality: explicit company guidance with a quoted range is worth far more than trend extrapolation because it embeds the order book and backlog conversion the company can actually see. One sigma of revenue history is $318m, and guidance narrows the plausible zone to roughly a third of that, so the guidance view moves the number most and is least likely to be wrong.

Every workstream

WorkstreamStateCitationsWhat would change it
mechanicalpass9a reported period that changes the historical series
guidancepass7Seeing the actual guided ranges the company gave for prior quarters (not just the final actuals) so I could compute the historical median landing position within guided ranges, rather than relying on qualitative pattern matching from a single guidance data point.
driverspass10A revision to the company's own Q3 guidance range, or a print of the September quarter's book to bill and utilization data showing utilization plateauing or reversing, would change the gross margin call. Any guidance update after the lock date, or an unexpected step change in mix toward lower margin Consumer or Communications end markets, would move the revenue and EPS estimates away from the guided midpoints.
demandabstained3Disclosures from ADI's major end markets, such as automotive OEM capex plans, industrial automation order books, or communications infrastructure spending guidance, and from ADI's foundry or substrate suppliers about wafer starts or lead times, would let me build an independent demand side estimate instead of abstaining.
marketpass8Independent, non ADI sourced data on analog and mixed signal semiconductor end market unit or revenue growth for calendar Q2 2026, for example SIA or WSTS shipment data or a peer company's independently reported segment growth, would let me separate ADI's own volume and mix driven share change from underlying market growth, rather than relying entirely on ADI's own guidance and historical self reported trend.
marginspass8A commentary from management indicating input cost inflation, unfavorable mix shift toward lower margin end markets, or a sequential dip in adjusted operating margin guidance below the 49.0% already reported would lower my gross margin estimate. Conversely, any interim guidance update raising the revenue or EPS outlook above the stated ranges would push my revenue and EPS estimates toward the top of guidance.
forensicspass10A widening rather than narrowing gap between GAAP and adjusted gross or operating margin in the next print would suggest the adjustments are being used to mask a structural cost increase rather than smooth a one off, which would make me discount the adjusted figures more heavily. Similarly, if the company begins excluding an item that has now recurred for four straight quarters, such as a restructuring or amortization charge previously called nonrecurring, that would be the strongest signal to revise down my confidence in the adjusted EPS and margin figures specifically.
peer readabstained3A disclosed quarterly report from an actual analog or mixed signal semiconductor peer, such as Texas Instruments, Microchip, NXP, or Infineon, covering a period overlapping ADI's fiscal third quarter (roughly February to May 2026), with revenue, margin, or bookings commentary on industrial, automotive, or communications end markets, would let me build a genuine peer based read across instead of abstaining.
macropass7A macro data feed showing a sudden downturn in semiconductor end-market demand (industrial, automotive, or communications capex pullback) during the quarter, or a company mid-quarter update revising guidance downward, would shift me toward the lower end of guidance ranges. Conversely, evidence of continued utilization gains and mix shift toward higher-margin industrial and automotive content would support gross margin above 73 percent and EPS above the guidance midpoint, closer to or above the street consensus mean.

03What the centre did+

Materiality of what each view rests on: forensics rests on two reported halves plus three reported quarters, so being wrong costs a few tens of millions at most; the mechanical projection rests on a series it evidently mis-scaled by an order of magnitude, so its error is total rather than marginal and it earns no weight. The three abstentions (demand, market, peer_read) removed the only checks external to the company, so the band was widened rather than tightened despite the surviving views' 0.25% coefficient of variation.

03What the centre did+

Materiality of the input each view rested on. The single largest swing factor for this metric is not the growth rate assumption (worth a few hundred million) but whether the anchor is equipment net sales or consolidated net sales and revenues (worth ~1,700m, over half a sigma). Only forensics priced that, so it earned the weight despite a 0.35 stated confidence; the three views resting on the 10,731.5 anchor were discounted to near zero on the level even though their growth logic was reused.

mechanicalpass9a reported period that changes the historical series

driverspass12A directly reported Q3 2025 Production and Precision Ag segment operating profit figure, or an actual preliminary Q3 2026 revenue or EPS print or updated company guidance narrowing the fiscal 2026 net income range, would materially change these estimates, since much of the reasoning here relies on inferred seasonal ratios rather than observed Q3 2025 segment data.
